source: NCERT Class XII, Fundamentals of Human Geography, Ch. 6 (Secondary Activities).

sections.heading: 1. Secondary Activities — Meaning
points: **Secondary activities** = those that **process raw materials into finished/more valuable goods (manufacturing)**.
They add value by changing the form of primary products (e.g. cotton → cloth, iron ore → steel).
Manufacturing ranges from **cottage/household industry** to **modern large-scale factories**.

sections.heading: 2. Types of Manufacturing
points: **Household/cottage** — smallest scale, family, simple tools, local market.
**Small-scale** — improved tools, some power, larger market.
**Large-scale** — factory system, machinery, mass production, wide market; needs large capital and labour.
By ownership: **public, private, joint, cooperative**; by product: **basic/heavy and consumer/light** industries.

sections.heading: 3. Factors of Industrial Location
points: **Access to raw materials, market, labour, power, capital, transport, and land**.
**Agglomeration economies** — industries cluster to share facilities (industrial regions).
Government policy, and increasingly **footloose industries** (e.g. electronics) that are not tied to raw materials.
Traditional heavy industries located near coal/iron (e.g. Ruhr, Damodar valley).

sections.heading: 4. Major Industries and Regions
points: **Iron and steel** — a basic industry (needs iron ore, coal, limestone).
**Textiles** (cotton, wool, silk, synthetic) — widespread, labour-intensive.
**Automobile, chemical, electronics, aircraft, food processing**.
Major industrial regions: **eastern North America, western/central Europe, eastern Europe, and eastern Asia (Japan, China, India)**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Secondary = manufacturing (process raw materials into finished goods).
Scale: household/cottage → small-scale → large-scale (factory).
Location factors: raw materials, market, labour, power, capital, transport.
Agglomeration economies = benefits of industries clustering.
Footloose industries (electronics) are not tied to raw materials.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Secondary activities = manufacturing** (adding value by changing form).
**Iron and steel is a basic/heavy industry** (near coal/iron ore).
**Footloose industries** can locate anywhere (not tied to raw materials).
**Agglomeration economies** arise when industries **cluster together**.
